questiontext.text:
\(A({@A[1]@},\,{@A[2]@},\,{@A[3]@})\) and \(B({@B[1]@},\,{@B[2]@},\,{@B[3]@})\). The point Q divides AB externally in the ratio \({@m@} : {@n@}\).

Find the position vector of Q.

\(\overrightarrow{OQ} =\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Externally, \(AQ : QB = {@m@} : {@n@}\) with Q on the line AB outside the segment, so \(\overrightarrow{AQ} = \dfrac{ {@m@} }{ {@m@} - {@n@} }\,\overrightarrow{AB} = [[if test="is(fq = 1)"]][[else]][[if test="is(fq = -1)"]]-[[else]]{@fq@}[[/if]][[/if]]\,\overrightarrow{AB}\). [[if test="is(m > n)"]]The fraction is greater than 1, so Q is beyond B.[[else]]The fraction is negative, so Q is beyond A.[[/if]]

\(\overrightarrow{AB} = {@vAB@}\), so \(\overrightarrow{AQ} = {@tAQ@}\) and \(\overrightarrow{OQ} = \overrightarrow{OA} + \overrightarrow{AQ} = {@tQ@}\).

questiondescription.text:
Vectors II: dividing a line externally

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.6: Find the position vector of a point dividing a line segment externally in a given ratio, beyond either end.

Core

This question is original to this project.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

truefeedback.text: That point is between A and B: it divides AB internally. For external division Q is outside the segment, so the length AB is the difference between AQ and QB, not their sum.
Your point divides AB externally in \({@n@} : {@m@}\), at the other end. \(AQ : QB = {@m@} : {@n@}\), so Q is beyond [[if test="is(m > n)"]]B[[else]]A[[/if]].
That point divides AB internally in the ratio \({@n@} : {@m@}\). Q divides AB externally in \({@m@} : {@n@}\), so it lies outside the segment AB.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="onl"]]

Your point is on the line AB, with \(\overrightarrow{AQ} = {@tq@}\,\overrightarrow{AB}\). So for your point \(AQ : QB = {@rr[1]@} : {@rr[2]@}\), which is not \({@m@} : {@n@}\).

[[else]]

Your point is not on the line AB: from A to your point is \(\begin{pmatrix} \displaystyle{@aq[1]@} \\ \displaystyle{@aq[2]@} \\ \displaystyle{@aq[3]@} \end{pmatrix}\), which is not a multiple of \(\overrightarrow{AB} = {@vAB@}\). Q is on the line AB, outside the segment, with \(AQ : QB = {@m@} : {@n@}\).

[[/if]]
